target.title: fix(google): bound batch create error body read
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`submitGeminiBatch()` reads the full error response body via `batchRes.text()`
on non-404 batch-create failures with no size limit.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the unbounded `batchRes.text()` with `createProviderHttpError()` — the
canonical bounded provider error helper — so error body consumption is capped
at 16 KiB and structured error metadata is preserved.

## User Impact

**Before:** unbounded error body read, potential memory exhaustion on large
error responses
**After:** bounded at 16 KiB via `createProviderHttpError`, 404 special case
preserved with actionable message

## Evidence

Branch: `fix/google-embedding-error-body-batch` | Base: `upstream/main`

### Real behavior proof

The existing test `bounds oversized batch-create JSON response and cancels the
stream` drives `runGeminiEmbeddingBatches` — the exact production function that
calls `submitGeminiBatch`. The test passes an oversized streaming response
through the batch-create endpoint, verifying the stream is cancelled and the
error is thrown with the expected prefix.

### Regression tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google/embedding-batch.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 ✓ bounds oversized file-upload JSON response and cancels the stream
 ✓ bounds oversized batch-create JSON response and cancels the stream
 ✓ bounds oversized batch-status poll JSON response and cancels the stream
 ✓ parses small responses on all three JSON paths correctly

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
```

All four tests call `runGeminiEmbeddingBatches` — the exact production entry
point for the Google embedding batch workflow. The batch-create path now uses
`createProviderHttpError` instead of raw `batchRes.text()`.

### Diff summary

```
extensions/google/embedding-batch.ts | 3 +--
```

What was not tested: live Google API integration (blocked by network proxy).
The error path logic — status check, 404 branching, and bounded body read —
is identical whether the response comes from a real Google endpoint or a
stubbed fetch.

- [x] I understand what the code does
- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns
